note: PREFERRED WORKING IDENTIFICATION, INFERRED FROM THE SAME RETROSPECTIVE WITNESS. Immediately beneath the exact keyed cut, Wentworth’s printed p. 86 states: “Gen. Beaubien’s house was near the N.-E. cor. Michigan Avenue and South-Water Street.” This explicitly associates the pictured house with the retrospective corner used by the sale-located homestead record and makes that record the preferred working identification over the separately modeled Factory House. It is Wentworth 1881, the same witness as the sale narrative, not independent corroboration or an 1831 survey. It does not establish whether the corner dwelling was a new residence or an earlier building, nor transfer the Factory House’s squared-log fabric or two storeys. HUBBARD’S CRITICISM IS PART OF THIS SAME PUBLICATION: his letter of 20 July 1881, pp. 86–87, says the cut is “certainly unlike the Fort and surroundings, as I recollect them.” He corrects the fort’s high ground, sharp point and river bends, blockhouse height and missing circa 1824–25 brick building. His suggestion that the sketch was engraved without Kinzie’s correction is explicitly probable, not proven. Do not distort surveyed positions or terrain to force this drawing. The credited 1831 view remains retrospective tier-5 form evidence, with survival to July 1835 unproved. No form measurements, camera, pictured-grade ruling or match verdict are added. The Wau-Bun-derived 1831 pair are not independent eyewitnesses. T-2378 GRAPHIC USE QUALIFICATION,2026-10-30: this conditional identity supported a diagnostic appearance comparison; a two-level mass, two main roof stacks, low front projection and small visible-gable light were accepted as bounded working proxies. This does not turn the drawing into a metric survey, attest paint/construction/pane counts, establish historical camera bearing or prove unchanged survival to July1835. The printed1857 credit and depicted1831 remain recorded separately from the verified1881 reproduction date.
